items.title: What the universe expands into
items.claim: When cosmologists say the universe is expanding, what is the most accurate description of where it expands to?

options.text: The metric of space itself increases distances between unbound objects; there is no external 'outside'

items.reveal_title: Expansion is of the metric, not into a container
items.reveal:
General relativity describes the metric of space evolving with time. The FLRW metric encodes this expansion.

Gravitationally bound systems (galaxies, the Local Group) are not expanding with the cosmic flow.
items.why: Cosmology requires letting go of everyday intuitions about space as a fixed stage.

items.title: Lemaitre before Hubble
items.claim: Hubble's 1929 paper reported a relationship between galaxy distance and redshift, indicating expansion. Who derived the relationship two years earlier?
items.reveal:
Lemaitre's 1927 paper in Annales de la Societe Scientifique de Bruxelles included an estimate of the expansion rate.

The IAU resolved in 2018 to refer to the law as the Hubble-Lemaitre Law.
items.why: Language and journal of publication shape who gets credited for foundational results.

items.title: JWST launch and arrival
items.claim: The James Webb Space Telescope launched on 25 December 2021. About how long to reach its operating point at L2?

options.text: About 30 days for L2 insertion; first science images released July 2022

items.reveal_title: About a month to L2; six months of commissioning before first science
items.reveal:
JWST inserted into L2 orbit on 24 January 2022. The first science images were released 12 July 2022.

The Sun-Earth L2 point lies about 1.5 million km from Earth.
items.why: Headline 'launch day' obscures months of staging required to make a telescope work.
